text:
ida: kicking off BanyanCorp LoRA onboarding. pushed a compact quick-eval to staging (job 5347). their data has a lot of tabular price lines and currency prefixes — heads-up for tokenization noise.
cheng: plan: fp16 -> int8 -> int4. capture QA_F1, exact_match, price_match (new heuristic), avg_latency. ETA ~2h.
omar: dropped a focused probe of 36 currency/price edgecases at /evals/banyan/price-probes-v1.json and flagged it on the job. includes patterns like 'USD1,200', '$ 1,200.00', '(1,234) JPY', and 'EUR 1.200,00' style.
rachel: fp16 baseline quickpass local: QA_F1=0.854, exact_match=0.69, price_match=0.96, avg_latency=74ms. snippet: ```json
{"job":"5347","phase":"fp16","metrics":{"qa_f1":0.854,"exact_match":0.69,"price_match":0.96,"avg_latency_ms":74}}
```
cheng: int8 run on staging pool done: QA_F1=0.847, exact_match=0.67, price_match=0.92, avg_latency=58ms. probe fails 8/36. common failure: missing space or removed comma in thousands.
ida: can you paste one raw fail sample? want to inspect tokenization.
cheng: sample: "Total due: USD 2,500" -> model output "USD2,500" (no space). our comparator flags it. seems like comma handling and spacing changes after quant.
omar: interesting edge: some locales use '.' as thousand sep and ',' as decimal. our probes include a few of those; need careful normalization.
ci-bot: staging job 5347 -> int4 run queued on node gpu-small-4 (ETA 11m).
rachel: I ran a quick token-diff offline and saw that int4 decodes sometimes emit a single token for 'USD2' + '500' pieces which our exact_match comparator treats strictly. looks like decode merging after quant. saving diffs to /tmp/token-diffs/5347-int4.txt.
ida: short-term mitigation idea: scoring normalizer that (a) removes interior thousands separators for scoring only, (b) enforces a single space between currency code and numeric token for comparator, and (c) does a locale fallback for '.' vs ',' decimals. low-risk and reversable.
cheng: agree. also log failing sample token ids to s3://redwood-debug/banyan/5347/fail-token-ids.log for debugging.
omar: I'll add a tiny eval-harness patch: `normalize_prices(text)` that runs before comparator; will open PR `banyan/normalize-prices`.
ida: decision proposal: promote int8 to canary, leave int4 as opt-in behind an experiment flag. add scoring normalizer (scoring-only), emit failing tokenids, and add a smoke repro command in tools. owners: cheng -> quant passes & CI, omar -> token diffs & s3 logging, rachel -> probe curation & metrics, ida -> rollout note + rollback.
cheng: added canonicalizer regex (one-liner): `text = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)[,](?=\d)", "", text); text = re.sub(r"(USD|EUR|JPY)\s*([0-9])", r"\\1 \\2", text)` and pushed to branch. running int8+int4 again.
ci-bot: job 5347 int8 re-run finished: QA_F1=0.850, probe_fail=3/36. int4 run started on gpu-small-4.
rachel: after normalizer patch: int8 QA_F1=0.850, probe fails 3/36 (mostly locale-variant decimals). int4 QA_F1=0.828, probe fails 6/36. normalizer removed majority of trivial tokenization mismatches.
omar: token-id dumps for failing int4 cases uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/banyan/5347/int4-tokenids.log. I also added smoke command: ```bash
# repro token merge locally
python tools/smoke_repro.py --model banyan-lora --sample 7 --quant int4
```
ops-bot: canary rule created: block promotion if price_match drops >1.5% vs baseline on probe set. alerting channel #eng-oncall.
ida: if int8 passes canary stable for 6h we'll promote. leaving int4 disabled by default until infra/research investigate decoder merge behavior. I'll draft a short runbook and release note stating canonicalizer is scoring-only and model outputs remain unchanged.
cheng: small follow-up: add a task to instrument embedding-space drift between fp16->int8->int4 on these failing samples. assign to infra-research.
rachel: noted. final metric snippet after patch: ```json
{"job":"5347","stage":"int8_post_norm","metrics":{"qa_f1":0.850,"price_match":0.945,"probe_fail":3}}
```
ida: thanks team. closing loop here — reopen if token-diff logs show systemic decoder rounding. :white_check_mark:
